name: metals
description: Scala language server with rich IDE features

viewsWelcome.contents:
No Scala project found. Create a new one or start Metals manually.
[New Scala project](command:metals.new-scala-project)

metals.disableReleaseNotes.markdownDescription: Do not show release notes when Metals was updated.

metals.forceCoursierJar.markdownDescription: Do not attempt to download/use Coursier executable and instead use fallback JAR in order to skip downloading from GitHub. It will try to download coursier jar from configured repositories. If Maven Central is not available make sure that your internal repository is properly configured.

metals.enableBestEffort.markdownDescription: When using Scala 3, use best effort compilation to improve Metals correctness when the workspace doesn't compile. Can be used instead of sourcepath based compilation.

metals.protobufLspEnabled.markdownDescription: If enabled, Metals will act as a Protobuf LSP server. Requires another extension to contribute the `proto` language and reloading the window.

metals.experimentalJarFileSystemEnabled.markdownDescription: Enable the experimental JAR filesystem provider (`jar-fs:`). When enabled, dependency sources opened from JARs use a real filesystem provider, which improves breadcrumbs and navigation. Requires reloading the window.

metals.defaultShell.markdownDescription: Optionally provide a default shell executable to use for build operations. This allows customizing the shell environment before build execution. When specified, it must be an absolute path to the shell. The configured shell will be used for all build-related subprocesses.

metals.serverVersion.markdownDescription:
The version of the Metals server artifact. Requires reloading the window.  

**VS Code extension version is guaranteed to work only with the default version, change if you know what you're doing**

metals.customServerLauncher.markdownDescription: Optional command to launch a Metals-compatible language server over standard input/output. When set, this completely overrides the default Metals server launch flow, including `metals.serverVersion`, `metals.serverProperties`, and `metals.customRepositories`.

metals.serverProperties.markdownDescription:
Optional list of properties to pass along to the Metals server. By default, the environment variable `JAVA_OPTS` and `.jvmopts` file are respected. Each property needs to be a separate item.

Example: `-Dhttps.proxyHost=…`, `-Dhttps.proxyPort=…` or `-Dmetals.statistics=all`

metals.coursierMirror.markdownDescription: Optional alternative repository to maven central if maven central is not available. For example: `https://jcenter.bintray.com`, which will be used to set to property described [here](https://get-coursier.io/blog/#mirrors)

metals.excludedPackages.markdownDescription:
Packages that will be excluded from completions, imports, and symbol searches.

This is in addition to some default packages that are already excluded. You can find the list of default exclusions [here on the Metals website](https://scalameta.org/metals/docs/editors/user-configuration/#excluded-packages).

Ex. `akka.actor.typed.javadsl` will ensure nothing in the `javadsl` package gets recommended to you.

If you need to remove one of the defaults, include it and preface it with `--`, for example `--sun`.

metals.inlayHints.inferredTypes.enable.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for inferred variable types and method return types.
```scala 

 val x/*: List[Int]*/ = List(1)
 def foo(x: Int)/*: Option[Int]*/ = Some(x)
```

metals.inlayHints.implicitArguments.enab.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for implicit arguments. 
```scala 

 given bar: Int = 123
 def foo(x: Int)(using Int) = ??? 
 foo(1)/*(using bar)*/
```

metals.inlayHints.implicitConversions.en.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for implicit conversions. 
```scala 

 implicit class MInt(i: Int) {
   def incr: Int = i + 1
 }
 val x = /*MInt(*/1/*)*/.incr 
```

metals.inlayHints.typeParameters.enable.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for type parameters. 
```scala 

 val x = List[Int](1)
 def foo[T](x: T) = x
 foo/*[Int]*/(1)
```

metals.inlayHints.hintsInPatternMatch.en.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints in pattern matches. 
```scala 

 case class Foo(a: Int, b: Int)
 val foo = Foo(1, 2)
 foo match {
   case Foo(a/*: Int*/, b/*: Int*/) =>
 }
```

metals.inlayHints.byNameParameters.enabl.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for by-name parameters. 
```scala 

 def foo(x: => Int) = ???
 foo(/*=> */1 + 2)
 foo {/*=> */
   val x = 1
   x + 1
 }
```

metals.inlayHints.namedParameters.enable.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for named parameters. 
```scala 

 def foo(number: Int) = ???
 foo(/*number = */1)
```

metals.inlayHints.hintsXRayMode.enable.markdownDescription:
Enable/disable inlay hints for x-ray like mode. 
```scala 

 val finalBar: Bar = foo
  .bar/*  : Bar*/
  .foo()/*: Foo*/
  .bar/*  : Bar*/
```

metals.javaHome.markdownDescription:
Optional path to the Java home directory that will be used for compiling the project.

Defaults to JDK used by Metals's server (look: Java Version).

This Java version should be lower or equal to JDK version used by the Metals's server.

metals.metalsJavaHome.markdownDescription:
Optional path to the Java home directory that will be used for the running Metals server.

By default Metals will try to infer it using the version specified in metals.javaVersion.

This Java version should be higher or equal to 17.

metals.javaVersion.markdownDescription:
JDK version used for running the Metals's server.

Should be greater or equal to the JDK version used for the project (look: Java Home).

metals.sbtScript.markdownDescription:
Optional absolute path to an `sbt` executable to use for running `sbt bloopInstall`.

By default, Metals uses `java -jar sbt-launch.jar` with an embedded launcher while respecting `.jvmopts` and `.sbtopts`.

Update this setting if your `sbt` script requires more customizations like using environment variables.

metals.millScript.markdownDescription:
Optional absolute path to a `mill` executable to use for running `mill mill.contrib.Bloop/install`.

By default, Metals uses an embedded `millw` script while respecting `.mill-version` file.

Update this setting if your `mill` script requires more customizations.

metals.mavenScript.markdownDescription:
Optional absolute path to a `mvn` executable to use for running `mvn ch.epfl.scala:maven-bloop_2.10:<bloop_version>:bloopInstall`.

By default, Metals uses an embedded `mvnw` script.

Update this setting if your `mvn` script requires more customizations.

metals.gradleScript.markdownDescription:
Optional absolute path to a `gradle` executable to use for running `gradle bloopInstall`.

By default, Metals uses an embedded `gradlew` script.

Update this setting if your `gradle` script requires more customizations.

metals.scalafmtConfigPath.markdownDescription:
Optional custom path to the .scalafmt.conf file.

Should be an absolute path and use forward slashes `/` for file separators (even on Windows).

metals.scalafixConfigPath.markdownDescription:
Optional custom path to the .scalafix.conf file.

Should be an absolute path and use forward slashes `/` for file separators (even on Windows).

metals.scalafixRulesDependencies.markdownDescription: Optional list of Scalafix rules dependencies to use for running `scalafix --rules`. For example: `com.github.liancheng::organize-imports:0.6.0`.

metals.scalafixLintEnabled.markdownDescription: When enabled, Scalafix rules from `.scalafix.conf` will be run on SemanticDB updates and lint diagnostics will be published alongside compiler diagnostics. Only lint diagnostics are shown; no code rewrites are applied.

metals.bloopVersion.markdownDescription: This version will be used for the Bloop build tool plugin, for any supported build tool, while importing in Metals.

metals.bloopJvmProperties.markdownDescription: Optional list of JVM properties to pass along to the Bloop server. Please follow [this guide](https://scalacenter.github.io/bloop/docs/server-reference#global-settings-for-the-server) for the format. Each property needs to be a separate item. The default is `-Xmx1G`.

metals.bloopSbtAlreadyInstalled.markdownDescription: If true, Metals will not generate `metals.sbt` files under the assumption that sbt-bloop is already manually installed in the sbt build. Build import will fail with a 'not valid command bloopInstall' error in case Bloop is not manually installed in the build when using this option.

metals.shutdownBloopOnEditorClose.markdownDescription: When enabled, when the last VS Code window with Metals is closed the extension will ask Metals to shut down the build server (Bloop). With multiple windows open, Bloop is only shut down when the last one closes. Machine-scoped because there is one Bloop process per machine. Disable if you run Bloop manually or want it to keep running after closing the editor.

metals.customRepositories.markdownDescription:
Optional list of custom resolvers passed to Coursier when fetching metals dependencies.

For documentation on accepted values see the [Coursier documentation](https://get-coursier.io/docs/other-repositories).

The extension will pass these to Coursier using the COURSIER_REPOSITORIES environment variable after joining the custom repositories with a pipe character (|).

metals.superMethodLensesEnabled.markdownDescription: Super method lenses are visible above methods that override another method. Clicking on a lens jumps to the super method definition. Disabled lenses are not calculated for opened documents, which might speed up document processing.

metals.enableStripMarginOnTypeFormatting.markdownDescription: When enabled, if you press the return key from the first line of a multiline string containing a pipe, it will automatically add `.stripMargin`.

metals.enableIndentOnPaste.markdownDescription: When this option is enabled, when a snippet is pasted into a Scala file, Metals will try to adjust the indentation to that of the current cursor.

metals.verboseCompilation.markdownDescription: If a build server supports it (for example Bloop or Scala CLI), setting it to true will make the logs contain all the possible debugging information, including information about incremental compilation in Zinc.

metals.enableSemanticHighlighting.markdownDescription: When this option is enabled, Metals will provide semantic tokens for clients that support it. The feature is still experimental and does not work for all sources.

enumDescriptions: Open `.class` files in the editor as usual.
Open with CFR decompiled Java (same as **Metals: Show decompiled Java**).
Open with javap disassembly (same as **Metals: Show javap**).
Open with javap verbose disassembly (same as **Metals: Show javap verbose**).
metals.classFileOpenEncoding.markdownDescription: When not `none`, opening a `.class` file uses a Metals custom editor and together with `workbench.editorAssociations` set VS Code does not treat the file as binary (no “Open anyway” prompt). The decoded view uses the same `metalsDecode:` pipeline as **Show decompiled Java** / **Show javap**.

metals.testUserInterface.markdownDescription:
Default way of handling tests and test suites. Valid values are `Code Lenses` and `Test Explorer`. See [the test explorer docs](https://scalameta.org/metals/docs/integrations/test-explorer) for information on how to work with the test explorer.

`Code Lenses` shows virtual text above a test class. `Test Explorer` shows gutter icons and a Testing panel that lists test suites in the workspace.

metals.testEnvironmentVariables.markdownDescription: Optional environment variables to pass to tests. Each key-value pair should be a separate item.

metals.customProjectRoot.markdownDescription: Optional relative path to your project's root. If you want your project root to be the workspace/workspace root set it to "." .

metals.fallbackScalaVersion.markdownDescription:
The Scala compiler version that is used as the default or fallback in case a file doesn't belong to any build target or the specified Scala version isn't supported by Metals. This applies to standalone Scala files, worksheets, and Scala CLI scripts.

The `automatic` value means that the Scala version for these files will be inferred from the highest supported Scala version in your project's build definition.

metals.eclipseFormat.configPath.markdownDescription: Optional custom path to the eclipse-formatter.xml file. It should be a path (relative or absolute, though an absolute path is recommended) and use forward slashes `/` for file separators (even on Windows).

metals.eclipseFormat.profile.markdownDescription: If the Eclipse formatter file contains more than one profile, this option can be used to control which is used.

metals.scalaCliLauncher.markdownDescription: Optional absolute path to a `scala-cli` executable to use for running a Scala CLI BSP server. By default, Metals uses the `scala-cli` from the PATH, or if it's not found, downloads and runs Scala CLI on the JVM (slower than native Scala CLI). Update this if you want to use a custom Scala CLI launcher that is not available in PATH.

enumDescriptions: Never suggest upgrades
Suggest upgrades with a notification popup
Automatically install latest version without asking
metals.suggestLatestUpgrade.markdownDescription: How to handle server version upgrades when a new version is available

metals.defaultBspToBuildTool.markdownDescription: If your build tool can also serve as a build server, default to using it instead of Bloop.

enumDescriptions: Prompt before importing a build.
Automatically import a build only when a project is first opened.
Automatically import a build on startup and after subsequent changes.
metals.autoImportBuilds.markdownDescription: Automatically import builds rather than prompting the user to choose. `initial` will only automatically import a build when a project is first opened, `all` will automate build imports after subsequent changes as well.

metals.startMcpServer.markdownDescription: If Metals should start the MCP server that an AI agent can connect to. The server speaks HTTP and can be used by AI tools to provide better context about the codebase. It also needs to be enabled in the client.

metals.symbolPrefixes.markdownDescription:
Prefix replacements used when printing symbols. You can replace package names with shorter ones to make them more readable.

Example: `{ "scala/": "scala-standard." }`.

metals.shimGlobs.markdownDescription:
Named groups of file glob patterns used to detect shim files in the presentation compiler. Entries follow the `glob` syntax of `FileSystem.getPathMatcher`, for example `**/shims.scala` to match all `shims.scala` files in the workspace. Values from all groups are combined into a single list.

Example: `{ "default": ["shims.scala", "**/shims/*.scala"] }`.

metals.gotoTestLensesEnabled.markdownDescription: Show code lenses that jump to tests.

metals.rangeFormattingProviders.markdownDescription: Providers used for range formatting. Valid values are `scalafmt`.

metals.worksheetCancelTimeout.markdownDescription: Seconds to wait before offering to cancel a worksheet.

enumDescriptions: Use the Eclipse Java formatter.
Use Google Java Format.
Disable Java formatting.
metals.javaFormatter.markdownDescription: The Java formatter to use. Valid values are `eclipse`, `googleJavaFormat`, or `none`. If `none` is specified, Java formatting will be disabled.

metals.scalaCliEnabled.markdownDescription: When enabled, Metals starts a Scala CLI server for standalone files.

metals.targetBuildTool.markdownDescription: The preferred build tool to use when multiple build definitions are detected in the workspace. This prevents the build tool selection dialog from appearing on startup. Valid values are `sbt`, `gradle`, `mvn`, `mill`, `scala-cli`, `bazel`, `deder`, and `none`.

metals.presentationCompilerDiagnostics.markdownDescription: Show presentation compiler errors and warnings as you type. This gives a much faster feedback loop but may show incorrect or incomplete error messages. Only supported in Scala 2.

enumDescriptions: Do nothing when build files change.
Prompt when build files change.
metals.buildChangedAction.markdownDescription: What to do when build files change. Valid values are `none` and `prompt`.

metals.buildOnChange.markdownDescription: If enabled, Metals will automatically build the project when a file changes.

metals.buildOnFocus.markdownDescription: If enabled, Metals will automatically build the project when a file is focused (opened).

metals.preferredBuildServer.markdownDescription: If set, Metals will prefer the specified build server when available instead of prompting the user.

enumDescriptions: Index sources from the BSP server.
Index sources from the git repository without requiring BSP.
metals.workspaceSymbolProvider.markdownDescription:
The workspace symbol provider to use. Valid values are `bsp` and `mbt`.

- `bsp`: The classic solution that only indexes sources from the BSP server.
- `mbt`: A BSP-free solution that indexes sources from the git repository.

metals.definitionProviders.markdownDescription: Definition providers. Valid values are `mbt`, `protobuf`, and `all`. By default all are enabled.

enumDescriptions: Load Java symbols from the Turbine classpath.
Load Java symbols from the Java source path.
metals.javaSymbolLoader.markdownDescription:
Java symbol loader to use when loading Java symbols in the Java presentation compiler.

- `turbine-classpath`: Loads Java symbols from the Turbine classpath.
- `javac-sourcepath`: Loads Java symbols from the Java source path.

metals.javaTurbineRecompileDelay.markdownDescription:
Delay before Turbine recompiles changed Java sources.

Example: `1 minute`.

metals.javaTurbineCache.markdownDescription: Persist Turbine compilation results between restarts.

metals.compilerProgress.markdownDescription: Compiler progress bars. Valid values are `enabled` and `disabled`.

enumDescriptions: Index sources based on SemanticDB documents.
Index sources from the git repository when SemanticDB documents are not available.
metals.referenceProvider.markdownDescription:
Reference provider to use when providing references to symbols in the presentation compiler.

- `bsp`: The classic solution that only indexes sources based on SemanticDB documents.
- `mbt`: A BSP-free solution that indexes sources from the git repository when SemanticDB documents are not available.

metals.additionalPcChecks.markdownDescription: Additional compiler phases to run in the presentation compiler. Valid values are `refchecks`. When `refchecks` is included, the presentation compiler will run the RefChecks phase for additional type checking diagnostics.

enumDescriptions: Append imports at the end of the import block.
Place imports based on prefix matching and alphabetical order.
metals.scalaImportsPlacement.markdownDescription:
Where to place new Scala imports. Valid values are `append-last` and `smart`.

- `append-last`: Append imports at the end of the import block.
- `smart`: Place imports intelligently based on prefix matching and alphabetical order.

metals.batchSemanticdbCompilerInstances.markdownDescription: Number of compiler instances used when generating SemanticDB in batch. This is useful to speed up SemanticDB generation when there are many files to process.

metals.promptBuildImport.markdownDescription: If enabled, Metals will prompt you to import or connect to a build server when a new workspace is detected. When disabled, you can still manually trigger import via the "Import build" command.

metals.mcpClient.markdownDescription:
Used when the client you are using does not match the editor, or when you also want an extra MCP config generated. For example, set this to `claude` if you use Claude Code in the terminal while Metals is running.

Metals generates an extra config when it supports the client you pass in, and still generates the config for your editor when that is also supported.

metals.mbt.importGeneratedSources.markdownDescription: If enabled, Metals will try to find the sources generated by the build tool during MBT import and include them as unchecked sources.

metals.mbt.semanticdbCacheEnabled.markdownDescription: If enabled, Metals will persist SemanticDB documents to disk in the `.metals/semanticdb-cache` directory. This can improve performance for find references and implementations in MBT mode by avoiding recalculating SemanticDB when files have not changed.

metals.mbt.semanticdbCacheMaxSize.markdownDescription: Maximum number of SemanticDB documents to keep in the in-memory cache. When this limit is exceeded, the least recently used documents are evicted.

metals.mbt.referencesTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Number of seconds to wait for references operations in MBT mode.

enumDescriptions: Do not use a fallback classpath.
Use all third-party dependencies.
Experimental. Try to guess the classpath based on the workspace.
Use the MBT classpath.
Use both MBT and all third-party dependencies.
metals.fallbackClasspath.markdownDescription: Fallback classpath providers. Valid values are `none`, `all3rdparty`, `guessed`, `mbt`, and `default`. `default` includes both MBT and all third-party dependencies. `guessed` is experimental and tries to guess the classpath based on the workspace.

enumDescriptions: Use all sources in the workspace.
Do not use any sources outside of existing build targets.
metals.fallbackSourcepath.markdownDescription:
Fallback sourcepath to use for sources outside of existing build targets.

- `allSources`: Use all sources in the workspace.
- `none`: Do not use any sources outside of existing build targets.

metals.trace.server.description: Traces the communication between VS Code and the Metals language server.
